title: Britannia Industries Ltd - 500825 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Britannia Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16.6% YoY to over ₹5,000 crore-level quarter, with 3.5% price hike taken and raw material inflation still elevated.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a decent quarter, with revenue from operations up 16.6% YoY and PAT at about 13% of revenue (PAT growth stated as 10.2%, with the transcript's figures inconsistent). Operating profit margin was about 17% and H1 revenue grew about 13.1%. General trade (GT) growth accelerated, with management saying it is trending near 7% in the latest period against 2.6% for FY26. Input costs were the main challenge: palm oil up 17% YoY, milk up 16% YoY, laminate up 18% YoY, sugar elevated, and wheat flour marginally down YoY. Britannia took a 3.5% price increase in the quarter, with further increases in the works.

financial_highlights.value: Stated as crossing ₹10,000 crore for the first time in the transcript, with a figure of 1,506 crore also quoted (unclear; transcript garbled)

financial_highlights.change: PAT growth stated as 10.2% YoY and 21.9% QoQ (figures inconsistent in transcript)
Low base (about minus 3% prior year) per analyst

segments.name: General trade (GT)
segments.commentary: Growth accelerated, with management citing a trend near 7% versus 2.6% for FY26; management said the base effect from the GST transition in September last year was worth at most 1.5-2% on the quarter.

segments.name: Modern trade and other channels
segments.commentary: Other channels, including modern trade and alternate channels, grew faster than GT; alternate channels trend significantly above GT.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: E-commerce at about 7% of sales; management said the share is understated because 5-rupee packs are hardly sold online, and urban e-commerce is already in double digits.

segments.name: Adjacencies (cakes, croissants, rusks)
segments.commentary: Grew more than 20%, with croissant and cake cited as star performers.

segments.name: Dairy
segments.commentary: Cheese is doing better, with flavoured slices introduced; drinks (Winking Cow) and ghee (Sattvam) are seeing traction.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Rest of international business grew in good double digits; Middle East pricing remains high due to costs.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to predict the future gross margin trajectory, citing uncertain input cost conditions.
Further price increases are in the works and will reach the market over time, with an implementation lag of about 1.5-2 months for shrink-led pricing.
The 3.5% price increase covers only part of the cost inflation; subsequent increases aim to close the gap.
Volume growth may be affected by planned gramage reductions, though management remains confident in its volume trajectory.
Management expects to launch health and protein-based platforms, with no timeline given to protect competitive positioning.
Management expects biscuits to keep growing strongly while non-biscuit portfolio gains share over time.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed in the call.
Britannia Nutrition Foundation reached about 5.73 lakh people, with women's participation in its plants at 48%.
demand_pricing: Price increase of 3.5% taken in the quarter, mainly on 5- and 10-rupee price points; management said these price points insulate biscuits from food inflation compared with peers.
Odd pricing (the 4.5-rupee point) has migrated to 5 and 10 rupees across the industry since around May-June 2026, per management.
Competition from Malkist in the cheese-cracker segment is intense; Britannia launched Cheese Dipped around December or January; Reliance Consumer's biscuit entry started in Tamil Nadu.
Management said GT consumption is resilient, with rural and semi-urban GT strong and premiumisation visible; metros and top-15 cities also decent.
Management said Britannia's per-kg realisation and raw material cost per kg are better than the market average, without giving figures.

qa_highlights.question: How should gross margins be considered, and is there further pricing beyond the 3.5% increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commodity inflation is elevated and here to stay, the 3.5% increase covers only part of cost inflation, and more price increases are in the works with a 1.5-2 month lag.

qa_highlights.question: Is 13% volume growth sustainable given the low base and gramage cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth of 13% is healthy on a low base, gramage reduction may weigh on volume, and transactions are growing well.

qa_highlights.question: Has Britannia regained market share after odd pricing and competition from Malkist and Reliance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said competition with Malkist is fierce but Britannia has dented its share; it regained shelf space; Reliance's entry in Tamil Nadu is being watched, and 5/10-rupee price points are harder to disrupt in biscuits than in snacks.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GT pick-up sustainable or a base effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the GST-transition base effect was at most 1.5-2%, GT consumption is resilient, rural and semi-urban are strong, and own execution is improving; growth is uniform across states.

qa_highlights.question: What is the e-commerce potential and how big can the channel grow?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce is at about 7% of sales, management is bullish, and it is being set up as a strategic business unit with product designed for the channel; premiumisation is the key opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the biscuit vs non-biscuit mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Biscuits are about 78-80% of the portfolio; non-biscuit categories are expected to grow faster over time.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from palm oil, milk, laminate and sugar inflation, with wheat outlook uncertain for next season.
Volume risk from gramage reductions and price-led growth.
Competitive intensity from Malkist in crackers and Reliance Consumer's biscuit entry in Tamil Nadu.
Milk prices not easing in winter, unlike typical seasonality, pressuring dairy and biscuit costs.
Management did not give timelines for health and protein platforms.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum, GT recovery and e-commerce, but cautious and deliberately non-committal on gross margin trajectory, input cost outlook and detailed unit economics.
key_quotes: So obviously the cost inflation is more than what and this is only covered part of it and our attempt with the subsequent increases is to close that gap.
So Britannia as an organization is extremely bullish on e-commerce.

growth.why: No numeric forward revenue guidance was given; the brief cites Q2 revenue up 16.6% YoY, a 3.5% price hike with further increases planned, volume growth of about 13% and GT trend near 7%, with no capacity additions, utilisation or capex disclosed, so backing is vague.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management declined to predict gross margin trajectory; palm oil up 17% YoY, milk up 16%, laminate up 18%, and the 3.5% price hike covers only part of cost inflation, with further increases still needed to close the gap.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed in the call.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volume grew about 13% in Q2 FY27 on a base of about minus 3% prior year and GT trend near 7% vs 2.6% in FY26, though planned gramage cuts may weigh on volume.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation and capex plans were not discussed, so no capex announcement signal can be read from the call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric forward guidance was given and management was non-committal on margins and input costs, so there is no clear basis for an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gross margin pressure from palm oil, milk, laminate and sugar inflation, with milk not easing in winter and wheat outlook uncertain, could pressure margins even as revenue grows about 16.6% YoY.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management expects health and protein platforms and flavoured cheese slices and drinks are gaining traction, but gave no timeline for the health and protein platforms.

rows.label: Further price increases to close cost gap
rows.why: The 3.5% hike covers only part of cost inflation, and further increases are in the works with a 1.5-2 month lag for shrink-led pricing.

rows.label: E-commerce and adjacencies scale-up
rows.why: E-commerce is about 7% of sales (up from about 6% in FY26), adjacencies grew more than 20%, and e-commerce is being set up as a strategic business unit.

rows.label: Competitive pressure in crackers and Tamil Nadu
rows.why: Malkist competition in cheese crackers is intense and Reliance Consumer's biscuit entry in Tamil Nadu is being watched, which could cap share gains.

tone.note: Management was confident on top-line momentum, GT recovery and e-commerce, but cautious and non-committal on gross margin, input cost outlook and unit economics; analysts pushed on whether the volume growth and GT pick-up were sustainable or base-driven.
